note: Queue rows the owner has resolved. build-resolution-queue.mjs removes these, so a resolved case cannot reappear the next time the queue is rebuilt.
why: The Resolution Center holds cases deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed. When the owner settles one it must leave the queue — but the queue is DERIVED, so the resolution has to live outside it or the next rebuild puts the row back. Same overlay pattern as claims-final.json, themes-owner-rulings.json, emphasis-owner-rulings.json and entities-owner-rulings.json.

resolved.resolution: Not a standalone notation token. [L] is one letter of the bracketed construction [L] [d] [R] running across the drop, which spells LDR — the same acrostic device Q uses in #129 and #4951. The queue asked 'what does [L] denote here?' and the answer is that it denotes nothing on its own; it marks a letter.
resolved.createsNoCategory: Deliberately no new certified category. The letters render as bracketed spans in the [ Brackets ] structure view, which is what a reader needs to see them.
resolved.emphasisNote: The owner ruled the #150 acrostic OUT of Emphasis earlier the same day, because both sentences are already certified — sentence 1 a Prediction, sentence 2 a Claim — so an Emphasis layer added no reading. This resolution therefore does NOT rest on a certified Emphasis row for #150; none exists. It rests on the construction being understood, which is what the queue was waiting on.
resolved.notCleared: code-15-_R_ (#1277, '[R] = Renegade') is a DIFFERENT case and stays queued. Q defines that [R] explicitly as a person; it is not part of the #150 construction. Clearing it because the token matches would be exactly the error the occurrence-identity rule exists to prevent.

resolved.resolution: Owner ruling: "Clinton's" here refers to Hillary AND Bill Clinton. Recorded as two entity mentions on #5 in audit/entities-owner-rulings.json — the queue asked which Clinton, and the answer is both.
resolved.notCleared: Only #5. Every other unattributed "Clinton" token stays queued; clearing them because the surname matches is exactly the error occurrence identity exists to prevent.

resolved.resolution: Owner ruling: NP here is a NON-PROFIT, not Nancy Pelosi. The line is "Why did Soros transfer his bulk public funds to a NP?" — the indefinite article makes it a category rather than a person, and #36 asks the identical question as "Why did Soros transfer the bulk of his 'public' funds to a NPO?". #5 also names "Pelosi" in full two lines earlier, so the drop had no need of an abbreviation for her.
resolved.createsNoCategory: Deliberately no new certified entity. "A non-profit" is a common noun — naming it as an Entity would put a category into a layer that holds specific named things. The queue asked what NP refers to; the answer is a kind of organisation, not one.
resolved.appliesAlsoTo: #6 carries the same line verbatim (a repost) and was never queued; the same reading holds there. No other NP occurrence is touched.
resolved.notCleared: NP-524-7-2 (#524 ">>NP [4] $8,000,000 Deutsche Bank USA") stays queued, along with the political-context occurrences in #436, #678, #1188, #1379 and #2075 where NP does read as Nancy Pelosi. Clearing them because the token matches is exactly the error occurrence identity prevents.

resolved.resolution: Owner ruling: Nancy Pelosi. The drop lists politicians against payments — Hussein, HRC/BC, NP — so the political reading is what the context supports here.
resolved.contrastWith: #5/#6, where the SAME token was ruled a non-profit ('transfer his bulk public funds to a NP?', with #36 asking it as 'a NPO?'). One token, two referents, decided by context — which is why rulings are recorded per occurrence and never as a global find-and-replace.
